title: Audit event serialization & contextualization guidelines for RBAC v2 and admin flows
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, implementable audit event serialization format and taxonomy that captures intent + context for RBAC v2 and admin operations (SSO/SAML flows, role changes, policy edits, key rotations). This doc prescribes event semantics (what to log), canonical fields, an efficient change encoding strategy for large objects (policies/roles), redaction and sampling rules, and retention tiering. Focus on: 1) consistent actor/target representation across services, 2) a compact yet searchable change encoding for later reconstruction and diffs, and 3) hooks for downstream consumers (analytics, alerting, legal requests).
comments: 2025-02-09: Initial draft completed. Included examples from role update and SAML provider rotation.
2025-02-11: Security review - Priya Patel: asked for stronger guidance on PII redaction and HSM references.
2025-02-14: Design sync with Console team - agreed on event tag 'ui_origin' and 'api_origin'.
2025-02-18: Infra feedback - Diego: suggested adding an optional 'change_digest' hash to speed lookups and dedupe.
2025-02-20: Updated encoding section to include field masks and op-based changes per infra feedback. Marked ready for implementation planning.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11234 (schema-to-proto) - awaiting review by eng-serialization team.
acceptance_criteria: Schema must include canonical actor and target fields used consistently by Console, Auth, and RBAC services.
Change encoding must be implementable as an op-path-value list and small enough to be stored inline for most policy edits (<= 2KB typical).
Events with redaction hints should not contain raw PII in plaintext in the primary event storage.
Downstream consumers can reconstruct the pre/post state using the ops and service links for up to 30 days.
Event envelope proto and REST contract are merged and a starter SDK serializer is provided in platform repo.
risks: Storing too much pre/post state increases storage costs and retention complexity.
Inconsistent actor identity shapes across services (user id vs external id) will make joins hard for analytics.
Complex policy objects could exceed the inline size target and require a secondary blob store lookup path.
Improper redaction implementation may leak PII to downstream consumers (logs, metrics).
next_steps: Finalize proto message and JSON schema by 2025-02-24.
Implement serializer in rbacs-service with toggle flag and integration tests (ENG-52911).
Add event export consumer test in observability pipeline to validate retention tiers and reconstructability.
Coordinate with Legal on long-term retention of admin change events for compliance requests.
